data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: accordingly
sections.question: accordingly
sections.summary: in a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances; as a result or consequence

senses.definition: in a way that is appropriate to the particular situation or circumstances
examples: She was told the dress code was formal and dressed accordingly.
There was a transport strike; accordingly, the meeting was postponed.

answers.answer: The manager explained the new safety rules and asked everyone to act accordingly.
She accordingly the report before submitting it to the senior management team.
He made an accordingly decision based on all the feedback he received from the team.
The team behaved accordingly to the rules that were set out at the start of the project.

sections.title: approximately
sections.question: approximately
sections.summary: used to show that a number, amount, or description is almost, but not completely, accurate

senses.definition: used to indicate that a value, quantity, or time is close to but not exactly what is stated
examples: The journey takes approximately two hours by train.
Approximately 500 people attended the conference last year.

answers.answer: There were approximately three hundred people at the outdoor concert last Saturday.
She gave an approximately answer when asked how far the station was from the hotel.
He approximately the total cost of the project before presenting his findings to the board.
The renovation cost approximately of five thousand pounds, including all labour and materials.

sections.title: consequently
sections.question: consequently
sections.summary: as a result of something that has just been mentioned; therefore

senses.definition: as a result of the situation just mentioned; therefore
examples: She missed several classes and consequently failed her final exam.
The factory closed; consequently, hundreds of workers lost their jobs.

answers.answer: He forgot to set his alarm and consequently missed the first session of the conference.
The report showed a consequently increase in profits following the company restructure.
She consequently the plan to ensure it would work within the reduced budget.
The rise in prices was consequently of the global shortage of raw materials.

sections.title: deliberately
sections.question: deliberately
sections.summary: done in a way that was planned or intended, not by accident; on purpose

senses.definition: done in a way that was planned or intended, not by accident
examples: She deliberately chose a quiet table at the back of the café to avoid being disturbed.
He deliberately ignored her messages to avoid having an argument.

answers.answer: She deliberately left the window open so the room would cool down before bedtime.
He made a deliberately mistake in the report to test whether anyone in the team noticed.
They spoke in a deliberately tone to make sure the audience grasped every point clearly.
She showed great deliberately in planning every last detail of the surprise farewell party.

sections.title: efficiently
sections.question: efficiently
sections.summary: in a way that achieves maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort, time, or resources

senses.definition: in a way that achieves maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort, time, or resources
examples: The new scheduling software allows the team to work much more efficiently.
She efficiently organised the department files so that anyone could find what they needed.

answers.answer: The new system allows customer complaints to be processed much more efficiently.
She showed great efficiently by completing all her tasks well before the deadline.
He wrote an efficiently report that greatly impressed the senior management team.
They efficiently to reduce costs across the department without affecting product quality.

sections.title: eventually
sections.question: eventually
sections.summary: in the end, especially after a long time or a lot of effort or problems

senses.definition: at the end of a long period of time or a series of events, especially after difficulties or delays
examples: After years of hard work, she eventually received the promotion she deserved.
He searched for over an hour and eventually found his keys in his coat pocket.

answers.answer: After several failed attempts, she eventually learned to drive and passed her test.
She was an eventually candidate for the role of team leader after her colleague retired.
They showed great eventually in completing the project despite all the setbacks they faced.
He eventually the final report and emailed it to the director just before the deadline.

sections.title: fortunately
sections.question: fortunately
sections.summary: used to say that a particular situation or outcome is good or lucky

senses.definition: used to express relief that something good has happened or that something bad has been avoided
examples: Fortunately, no one was hurt in the accident.
I forgot my umbrella, but fortunately it didn't rain during the walk home.

answers.answer: Fortunately, she remembered her passport just before leaving for the airport.
She felt fortunately about the outcome of the interview and expected to receive a job offer.
The fortunately result was that the storm passed before the outdoor event had to begin.
He showed great fortunately when he heard that he had passed all his final exams.

sections.title: frequently
sections.question: frequently
sections.summary: often; happening many times at short intervals

senses.definition: happening or occurring often; many times at short intervals
examples: She frequently visits her parents at the weekend.
Buses run frequently on this route during the morning rush hour.

answers.answer: He frequently checks his messages throughout the day to stay on top of his workload.
They go on frequently business trips to meet their international clients in person.
She showed great frequently in attending every optional training session that was offered.
The team frequently their working methods each month to try to improve overall results.

sections.title: significantly
sections.question: significantly
sections.summary: in a way that is important or large enough to have a noticeable effect on a situation

senses.definition: in a way that is large or important enough to have a clear effect on a situation or to be easily noticed
examples: Prices have increased significantly over the past two years.
The new treatment significantly reduced the patient's recovery time.

answers.answer: The new training programme has significantly improved the performance of the entire team.
The results showed a significantly improvement in overall customer satisfaction scores.
She showed great significantly in her research findings and was praised by her supervisor.
He significantly his position on the matter to avoid further conflict with the management.

sections.title: typically
sections.question: typically
sections.summary: in a way that is usual or expected; used to describe what normally happens in a particular situation

senses.definition: in a way that shows the usual or expected qualities of a particular person, thing, or group
examples: British weather is typically unpredictable throughout the spring months.
A full-time position typically involves working around forty hours per week.

answers.answer: British people typically queue politely and wait their turn without complaint.
She showed a typically enthusiasm for the new project that greatly impressed her manager.
He felt typically about the changes introduced by the new senior management team.
The manager typically the weekly schedule to ensure all workloads were evenly balanced.
